summary:
Turn 92 closed the run's local work on the exhausted capacities, with the frontier reduced to a short documented residue.

Why a scoped stop rather than more work. Two capacities are exhausted: audit units (no further obligation can be opened) and semantic reviews, which means the newest artifact — the end-to-end client-reply scenario for the owner-alive re-proposal protection, executed as 6baf5b7715294d88a8f4a36e085ebd04 — cannot receive the correspondence review that would confirm it and therefore stays visible as an unreviewed execution rather than being claimed. Experiments and calls remain, but the frontier is no longer unexplored code: every file named in the run's analysis roots has been read, the map is current at version 19, and the outstanding items are deployment or framework questions rather than investigation targets. The stop is scoped to the focus, so unfinished units and disputes remain visible instead of being closed by it.

Where the audit stands. Twelve claim families were established, each with its own obligation, bindings, plan and executed artifacts: nine confirmed violations or consequences — C1 (a recovery ignores a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED and commits a NOOP vector for it, on a driven proposal/commit history), C3 (the same divergence reaching the applied state, also on a driven history), C2 (the durable metadata record loses the bal value it writes), C4 (a legal NOOP commit terminates a restarted owner through a nil dereference, on a constructed history), C6 (the same recovery divergence for the deployment's promoted replica), C7 (the accept handler's rejection branch is unreachable, so a rejected round waits for the timeout), C9 (the recorder writes the recovering replica's own row's metadata, or dereferences nothing), C10 (a value beyond the 16-bit length field is truncated, displaces the following commands, and panics the receiver's decoder), C11 (replica construction dereferences a failed probe dial, so an environment without a route to the probe cannot start a replica), C12 (the documented transitive-conflict skipping is inert) — plus two bounded no-violation protections: C5 (an owner that survives a NOOP recovery re-proposes the operation and, as of the newest artifact, answers the client end to end) and C8 (the executor's timeout enqueues a blocked instance and the enqueued entry starts a real recovery).

Residue recorded rather than absorbed. The reader-side reaction to a displaced stream cannot be exercised from an in-package harness because the replica package's listener is unexported, so it stays a source-based inference. Whether a deployment enables the latency file, durable recording or the transitive-skip flag decides whether those findings are live, and that is a configuration question. Two candidates remain paused with scoped resume conditions (accept-status semantics, client retry), and one attribution issue on the superseded C1 artifact has no mechanism the validator accepts, so it remains visible as bookkeeping with its substance already recorded in the amended claim and in C3. Resume conditions for the stopped focus name the missing review capacity, the unit capacity a new obligation would need, and the configurations that would activate the remaining paths.
